descriptionChirho: To reach, arrive at, or attain; an Aramaic verb occurring exclusively in Daniel. Used of Nebuchadnezzar's great tree whose height 'reached' (יִמְטֵא) to heaven (Dan 4:11, 20), of a decree that 'came' (מְּטָא) upon the king (Dan 4:28), of a vision whose time 'reached/arrived' (מְטָת, 3fs; Dan 4:24), of dominion that 'reached' (מְטָה) to the end of the earth (Dan 7:13, 22), and of accusers who 'reached' (מְטוֹ, 3mp) the bottom of the den (Dan 6:24). All Qal inflectional forms of the same verb root. Multilingual glosses converge: arb بَلَغَ/يَبْلُغُ/وَصَلَ (arrive/reach), hin पहुंचा/आया (arrive/come), kor 이르렀다/닿았다 (arrived/reached), spa llego/alcanzo.
